analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset` obtains an attacker-controlled compressed-offsets pointer from the in-memory frame and passes it to the legacy `blosc_getitem` API without supplying or validating the available offsets-chunk length. `blosc_getitem` consequently calls `_blosc_getitem` with `srcsize == INT32_MAX`; a forged block-start offset is treated as in bounds, and `blosc_d` reads a 32-bit compressed-stream size beyond the actual frame allocation. The ASan read in `sw32_` is the downstream crash. The caller should derive and validate the offsets region size (including its chunk header/cbytes) and use a size-aware getitem/decompression path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The harness opens the fuzzer bytes as an in-memory sframe and decompresses chunk 0. The frame must pass the minimal frame-length/trailer marker checks and expose at least one logical chunk, while malformed header values place the coffsets region at attacker-controlled bytes. In this PoV, `header_len == 0` and `cbytes == 0`, so `get_coffsets` returns the start of the 89-byte input as if it were a compressed offsets chunk. Its forged Blosc header yields a block start of 89 (exactly one byte past the allocation). Because `blosc_getitem` advertises `INT32_MAX` bytes, the offset passes its checks and `blosc_d` performs the 4-byte out-of-bounds read at input+89.
